newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish investment group creates private power firm.
newsitem.headline: Polish investment group creates private power firm.

text.p: Polish-based group Enterprise Investors Sp zoo has created the country's first private power sector firm, in which it aims to invest $15 million within three years, its president said on Monday.

Enterprise Investors, comprised of four Polish-based investment funds, said the new Polish Energy Partners SA (PEP) firm would build and modernise power plants as well as energy distribution in Poland.
"We plan to invest up to $15 million, hopefully within a very short period of time... of about three years," Enterprise Investors' President Michal Rusiecki told a news conference.

Rusiecki expected that up to $100 million in total would be invested in PEP in the next three years, with around 80 percent of the capital coming from private investors. He declined to give details of what investors would be involved.
PEP President Wojciech Cetnarski told the conference that the company would initially concentrate on power engineering for large Polish industrial firms and later on meeting municipal power needs.
The four funds administered by Enterprise Investors are the Polish Enterprise Fund, the Polish Private Equity Fund I and II and the Polish-American Enterprise Fund.
It said in a statement that it has already invested over $450 million in Poland's economy.
